units.leftText: We will not give our daughters in marriage to the people of the land, and we will not take their daughters for our sons.
units.rightText: and that we would not give our daughters unto the peoples of the land, nor take their daughters for our sons;

units.leftText: When the people of the land bring merchandise or any kind of grain to sell on the Sabbath day, we will not buy from them on a Sabbath or holy day. Every seventh year we will let the fields lie fallow and will cancel every debt.
units.rightText: and if the peoples of the land bring wares or any grain on the sabbath day to sell, that we would not buy of them on the sabbath, or on a holy day; and that we would forego the seventh year, and the exaction of every debt.

units.leftText: We also place ourselves under the obligation to contribute a third of a shekel yearly for the service of the house of our God:
units.rightText: Also we made ordinances for us, to charge ourselves yearly with the third part of a shekel for the service of the house of our God;
leftNotes: 10:32 A third of a shekel is approximately 0.13 ounces or 3.8 grams, probably of silver.

units.leftText: for the showbread, for the regular grain offerings and burnt offerings, for the Sabbath offerings, for the New Moons and appointed feasts, for the holy offerings, for the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and for all the duties of the house of our God.
units.rightText: for the showbread, and for the continual meal-offering, and for the continual burnt-offering, for the sabbaths, for the new moons, for the set feasts, and for the holy things, and for the sin-offerings to make atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.

units.leftText: We have cast lots among the priests, Levites, and people for the donation of wood by our families at the appointed times each year. They are to bring it to the house of our God to burn on the altar of the LORD our God, as it is written in the Law.
units.rightText: And we cast lots, the priests, the Levites, and the people, for the wood-offering, to bring it into the house of our God, according to our fathers’ houses, at times appointed, year by year, to burn upon the altar of Jehovah our God, as it is written in the law;

units.leftText: We will also bring the firstfruits of our land and of every fruit tree to the house of the LORD year by year.
units.rightText: and to bring the first-fruits of our ground, and the first-fruits of all fruit of all manner of trees, year by year, unto the house of Jehovah;

units.leftText: And we will bring the firstborn of our sons and our livestock, as it is written in the Law, and will bring the firstborn of our herds and flocks to the house of our God, to the priests who minister in the house of our God.
units.rightText: also the first-born of our sons, and of our cattle, as it is written in the law, and the firstlings of our herds and of our flocks, to bring to the house of our God, unto the priests that minister in the house of our God;

units.leftText: Moreover, we will bring to the priests at the storerooms of the house of our God the firstfruits of our dough, of our grain offerings, of the fruit of all our trees, and of our new wine and oil. A tenth of our produce belongs to the Levites, so that they shall receive tithes in all the towns where we labor.
units.rightText: and that we should bring the first-fruits of our dough, and our heave-offerings, and the fruit of all manner of trees, the new wine and the oil, unto the priests, to the chambers of the house of our God; and the tithes of our ground unto the Levites; for they, the Levites, take the tithes in all the cities of our tillage.

units.leftText: A priest of Aaron’s line is to accompany the Levites when they collect the tenth, and the Levites are to bring a tenth of these tithes to the storerooms of the treasury in the house of our God.
units.rightText: And the priest the son of Aaron shall be with the Levites, when the Levites take tithes: and the Levites shall bring up the tithe of the tithes unto the house of our God, to the chambers, into the treasure-house.

units.leftText: For the Israelites and the Levites are to bring the contributions of grain, new wine, and oil to the storerooms where the articles of the sanctuary are kept and where the ministering priests, the gatekeepers, and the singers stay. Thus we will not neglect the house of our God.”
units.rightText: For the children of Israel and the children of Levi shall bring the heave-offering of the grain, of the new wine, and of the oil, unto the chambers, where are the vessels of the sanctuary, and the priests that minister, and the porters, and the singers: and we will not forsake the house of our God.

units.leftText: Now the leaders of the people settled in Jerusalem, and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of ten to live in the holy city of Jerusalem, while the remaining nine were to dwell in their own towns.
units.rightText: And the princes of the people dwelt in Jerusalem: the rest of the people also cast lots, to bring one of ten to dwell in Jerusalem the holy city, and nine parts in the other cities.
leftNotes: 11:1 Hebrew nine hands

units.leftText: And the people blessed all the men who volunteered to live in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And the people blessed all the men that willingly offered themselves to dwell in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: These are the heads of the provinces who settled in Jerusalem. (In the villages of Judah, however, each lived on his own property in their towns— the Israelites, priests, Levites, temple servants, and descendants of Solomon’s servants—
units.rightText: Now these are the chiefs of the province that dwelt in Jerusalem: but in the cities of Judah dwelt every one in his possession in their cities, to wit, Israel, the priests, and the Levites, and the Nethinim, and the children of Solomon’s servants.
leftNotes: 11:3 Hebrew Nethinim; also in verse 21

units.leftText: while some of the descendants of Judah and Benjamin settled in Jerusalem.) From the descendants of Judah:
units.rightText: And in Jerusalem dwelt certain of the children of Judah, and of the children of Benjamin. Of the children of Judah: Athaiah the son of Uzziah, the son of Zechariah, the son of Amariah, the son of Shephatiah, the son of Mahalalel, of the children of Perez;

units.leftText: and Maaseiah son of Baruch, the son of Col-hozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, a descendant of Shelah.
units.rightText: and Maaseiah the son of Baruch, the son of Col-hozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, the son of the Shilonite.
leftNotes: 11:5 Or of the Shilonite

units.leftText: The descendants of Perez who settled in Jerusalem totaled 468 men of valor.
units.rightText: All the sons of Perez that dwelt in Jerusalem were four hundred threescore and eight valiant men.

units.leftText: From the descendants of Benjamin:
units.rightText: And these are the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Joed, the son of Pedaiah, the son of Kolaiah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Jeshaiah.

units.leftText: and his followers Gabbai and Sallai — 928 men.
units.rightText: And after him Gabbai, Sallai, nine hundred twenty and eight.

units.leftText: Joel son of Zichri was the officer over them, and Judah son of Hassenuah was over the Second District of the city.
units.rightText: And Joel the son of Zichri was their overseer; and Judah the son of Hassenuah was second over the city.
leftNotes: 11:9 Or was over the Second Quarter of the city, a newer section of Jerusalem; or was second in command of the city

units.leftText: From the priests:
units.rightText: Of the priests: Jedaiah the son of Joiarib, Jachin,

units.leftText: Seraiah son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the chief official of the house of God;
units.rightText: Seraiah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the ruler of the house of God,

units.leftText: and their associates who did the work at the temple — 822 men;
units.rightText: and their brethren that did the work of the house, eight hundred twenty and two; and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pelaliah, the son of Amzi, the son of Zechariah, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah,

units.leftText: and his associates, the leaders of families — 242 men;
units.rightText: and his brethren, chiefs of fathers’ houses, two hundred forty and two; and Amashsai the son of Azarel, the son of Ahzai, the son of Meshillemoth, the son of Immer,

units.leftText: and his associates — 128 mighty men of valor. Zabdiel son of Haggedolim was their overseer.
units.rightText: and their brethren, mighty men of valor, a hundred twenty and eight; and their overseer was Zabdiel, the son of Haggedolim.
leftNotes: 11:14 Most LXX manuscripts; Hebrew their associates

units.leftText: From the Levites:
units.rightText: And of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Bunni;

units.leftText: Shabbethai and Jozabad, two leaders of the Levites, who supervised the work outside the house of God;
units.rightText: and Shabbethai and Jozabad, of the chiefs of the Levites, who had the oversight of the outward business of the house of God;

units.leftText: Mattaniah son of Mica, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaph, who led in thanksgiving and prayer; Bakbukiah, second among his associates; and Abda son of Shammua, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun.
units.rightText: and Mattaniah the son of Mica, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaph, who was the chief to begin the thanksgiving in prayer, and Bakbukiah, the second among his brethren; and Abda the son of Shammua, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun.

units.leftText: The Levites in the holy city totaled 284.
units.rightText: All the Levites in the holy city were two hundred fourscore and four.

units.leftText: And the gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon, and their associates, who kept watch at the gates — 172 men. Residents Outside Jerusalem
units.rightText: Moreover the porters, Akkub, Talmon, and their brethren, that kept watch at the gates, were a hundred seventy and two.

units.leftText: The rest of the Israelites, with the priests and Levites, were in all the villages of Judah, each on his own inheritance.
units.rightText: And the residue of Israel, of the priests, the Levites, were in all the cities of Judah, every one in his inheritance.

units.leftText: The temple servants lived on the hill of Ophel, with Ziha and Gishpa over them.
units.rightText: But the Nethinim dwelt in Ophel: and Ziha and Gishpa were over the Nethinim.

units.leftText: Now the overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Mica. He was one of Asaph’s descendants, who were the singers in charge of the service of the house of God.
units.rightText: The overseer also of the Levites at Jerusalem was Uzzi the son of Bani, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Mica, of the sons of Asaph, the singers, over the business of the house of God.
leftNotes: 11:22 Mica is a variant of Micaiah; see Nehemiah 12:35|NEH 12:35*.

units.leftText: For there was a command from the king concerning the singers, an ordinance regulating their daily activities.
units.rightText: For there was a commandment from the king concerning them, and a settled provision for the singers, as every day required.

units.leftText: Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, a descendant of Zerah son of Judah, was the king’s agent in every matter concerning the people.
units.rightText: And Pethahiah the son of Meshezabel, of the children of Zerah the son of Judah, was at the king’s hand in all matters concerning the people.
leftNotes: 11:24 Hebrew hand

units.leftText: As for the villages with their fields, some of the people of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba, Dibon, Jekabzeel, and their villages;
units.rightText: And as for the villages, with their fields, some of the children of Judah dwelt in Kiriath-arba and the towns thereof, and in Dibon and the towns thereof, and in Jekabzeel and the villages thereof,

units.leftText: in Jeshua, Moladah, and Beth-pelet;
units.rightText: and in Jeshua, and in Moladah, and Beth-pelet,

units.leftText: in Hazar-shual; in Beersheba and its villages;
units.rightText: and in Hazar-shual, and in Beer-sheba and the towns thereof,

units.leftText: in Ziklag; in Meconah and its villages;
units.rightText: and in Ziklag, and in Meconah and in the towns thereof,

units.leftText: in En-rimmon, Zorah, Jarmuth,
units.rightText: and in En-rimmon, and in Zorah, and in Jarmuth,

units.leftText: Zanoah, Adullam, and their villages; in Lachish and its fields; and in Azekah and its villages. So they settled from Beersheba all the way to the Valley of Hinnom.
units.rightText: Zanoah, Adullam, and their villages, Lachish and the fields thereof, Azekah and the towns thereof. So they encamped from Beer-sheba unto the valley of Hinnom.

units.leftText: The descendants of Benjamin from Geba lived in Michmash, Aija, and Bethel with its villages;
units.rightText: The children of Benjamin also dwelt from Geba onward, at Michmash and Aija, and at Beth-el and the towns thereof,

units.leftText: in Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
units.rightText: at Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,

units.leftText: Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
units.rightText: Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,

units.leftText: Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
units.rightText: Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,

units.leftText: Lod, and Ono; and in the Valley of the Craftsmen.
units.rightText: Lod, and Ono, the valley of craftsmen.
leftNotes: 11:35 Hebrew in Ge-harashim

units.leftText: And some divisions of the Levites of Judah settled in Benjamin.
units.rightText: And of the Levites, certain courses in Judah were joined to Benjamin.

units.leftText: Now these are the priests and Levites who went up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and with Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
units.rightText: Now these are the priests and the Levites that went up with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,

units.leftText: Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
units.rightText: Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
leftNotes: 12:2 Malluch is a variant of Malluchi; see verse 14.

units.leftText: Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
units.rightText: Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
leftNotes: 12:3 Rehum is a variant of Harim; see verse 15, Nehemiah 7:42|NEH 7:42*, and Ezra 2:39.

units.leftText: Iddo, Ginnethon, Abijah,
units.rightText: Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
leftNotes: 12:4 Many Hebrew manuscripts and Vulgate (see also verse 16); most MT manuscripts Ginnethoi

units.leftText: Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
units.rightText: Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
leftNotes: 12:5 Mijamin is a variant of Miniamin; see verse 17.
12:5 Maadiah is a variant of Moadiah; see verse 17.
12:5 Bilgah is a variant of Bilgai; also in verse 18; see Nehemiah 10:8|NEH 10:8*.

units.leftText: Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,
units.rightText: Shemaiah, and Joiarib, Jedaiah.

units.leftText: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah. These were the leaders of the priests and their associates in the days of Jeshua.
units.rightText: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah. These were the chiefs of the priests and of their brethren in the days of Jeshua.

units.leftText: The Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, who, with his associates, led the songs of thanksgiving.
units.rightText: Moreover the Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, who was over the thanksgiving, he and his brethren.

units.leftText: Bakbukiah and Unni, their associates, stood across from them in the services.
units.rightText: Also Bakbukiah and Unno, their brethren, were over against them according to their offices.

units.leftText: Jeshua was the father of Joiakim, Joiakim was the father of Eliashib, Eliashib was the father of Joiada,
units.rightText: And Jeshua begat Joiakim, and Joiakim begat Eliashib, and Eliashib begat Joiada,

units.leftText: Joiada was the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan was the father of Jaddua.
units.rightText: and Joiada begat Jonathan, and Jonathan begat Jaddua.
leftNotes: 12:11 Jonathan is a variant of Johanan; see verse 22.

units.leftText: In the days of Joiakim, these were the heads of the priestly families: of the family of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;
units.rightText: And in the days of Joiakim were priests, heads of fathers’ houses: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;

units.leftText: of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan;
units.rightText: of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan;

units.leftText: of Malluchi, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph;
units.rightText: of Malluchi, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph;
leftNotes: 12:14 Malluchi is a variant of Malluch; see verse 2.
12:14 Shebaniah is a variant of Shecaniah; see verse 3; see also Syriac and some Hebrew and LXX manuscripts.

units.leftText: of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai;
units.rightText: of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai;
leftNotes: 12:15 Meraioth is a variant of Meremoth; see verse 3 and also some LXX manuscripts.

units.leftText: of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam;
units.rightText: of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam;

units.leftText: of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin and of Moadiah, Piltai;
units.rightText: of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin, of Moadiah, Piltai;
leftNotes: 12:17 Moadiah is a variant of Maadiah; see verse 5.

units.leftText: of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jonathan;
units.rightText: of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan;

units.leftText: of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;
units.rightText: and of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;

units.leftText: of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber;
units.rightText: of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber;
leftNotes: 12:20 Sallai is a variant of Sallu; see verse 7.

units.leftText: of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; and of Jedaiah, Nethanel.
units.rightText: of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethanel.

units.leftText: In the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, during the reign of Darius the Persian, the heads of the families of the Levites and priests were recorded.
units.rightText: As for the Levites, in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, and Johanan, and Jaddua, there were recorded the heads of fathers’ houses; also the priests, in the reign of Darius the Persian.
leftNotes: 12:22 Johanan is a variant of Jonathan; see verse 11.

units.leftText: As for the descendants of Levi, the family heads up to the days of Johanan son of Eliashib were recorded in the Book of the Chronicles.
units.rightText: The sons of Levi, heads of fathers’ houses, were written in the book of the chronicles, even until the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib.
leftNotes: 12:23 Or the Book of the Annals or the Book of the Historical Events

units.leftText: The leaders of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua son of Kadmiel, along with their associates, who stood across from them to give praise and thanksgiving as one section alternated with the other, as prescribed by David the man of God.
units.rightText: And the chiefs of the Levites: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua the son of Kadmiel, with their brethren over against them, to praise and give thanks, according to the commandment of David the man of God, watch next to watch.
leftNotes: 12:24 Or Sherebiah, Jeshua, Binnui, and Kadmiel

units.leftText: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers who guarded the storerooms at the gates.
units.rightText: Mattaniah, and Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, Akkub, were porters keeping the watch at the store-houses of the gates.

units.leftText: They served in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and scribe. The Dedication of the Wall
units.rightText: These were in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest the scribe.
leftNotes: 12:26 Jozadak is a variant of Jehozadak; see 1 Chronicles 6:14|1CH 6:14*.

units.leftText: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, the Levites were sought out from all their homes and brought to Jerusalem to celebrate the joyous dedication with thanksgiving and singing, accompanied by cymbals, harps, and lyres.
units.rightText: And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought the Levites out of all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem, to keep the dedication with gladness, both with thanksgivings, and with singing, with cymbals, psalteries, and with harps.

units.leftText: The singers were also assembled from the region around Jerusalem, from the villages of the Netophathites,
units.rightText: And the sons of the singers gathered themselves together, both out of the plain round about Jerusalem, and from the villages of the Netophathites;

units.leftText: from Beth-gilgal, and from the fields of Geba and Azmaveth, for they had built villages for themselves around Jerusalem.
units.rightText: also from Beth-gilgal, and out of the fields of Geba and Azmaveth: for the singers had builded them villages round about Jerusalem.

units.leftText: After the priests and Levites had purified themselves, they purified the people, the gates, and the wall.
units.rightText: And the priests and the Levites purified themselves; and they purified the people, and the gates, and the wall.

units.leftText: Then I brought the leaders of Judah up on the wall, and I appointed two great thanksgiving choirs. One was to proceed along the top of the wall to the right, toward the Dung Gate.
units.rightText: Then I brought up the princes of Judah upon the wall, and appointed two great companies that gave thanks and went in procession; whereof one went on the right hand upon the wall toward the dung gate:
leftNotes: 12:31 Or alongside the wall; also in verse 38

units.leftText: Hoshaiah and half the leaders of Judah followed,
units.rightText: and after them went Hoshaiah, and half of the princes of Judah,

units.leftText: along with Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,
units.rightText: and Azariah, Ezra, and Meshullam,

units.leftText: Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, Jeremiah,
units.rightText: Judah, and Benjamin, and Shemaiah, and Jeremiah,

units.leftText: and some of the priests with trumpets, and also Zechariah son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Micaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph,
units.rightText: and certain of the priests’ sons with trumpets: Zechariah the son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Micaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph;
leftNotes: 12:35 Micaiah is a variant of Mica; see Nehemiah 11:22|NEH 11:22*.

units.leftText: and his associates— Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani— with the musical instruments prescribed by David the man of God. Ezra the scribe led the procession.
units.rightText: and his brethren, Shemaiah, and Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, and Judah, Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God; and Ezra the scribe was before them.

units.leftText: At the Fountain Gate they went directly up the steps of the City of David on the ascent to the wall and passed above the house of David to the Water Gate on the east.
units.rightText: And by the fountain gate, and straight before them, they went up by the stairs of the city of David, at the ascent of the wall, above the house of David, even unto the water gate eastward.

units.leftText: The second thanksgiving choir proceeded to the left, and I followed it with half the people along the top of the wall, past the Tower of the Ovens to the Broad Wall,
units.rightText: And the other company of them that gave thanks went to meet them, and I after them, with the half of the people, upon the wall, above the tower of the furnaces, even unto the broad wall,

units.leftText: over the Gate of Ephraim, the Jeshanah Gate, the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate. And they stopped at the Gate of the Guard.
units.rightText: and above the gate of Ephraim, and by the old gate, and by the fish gate, and the tower of Hananel, and the tower of Hammeah, even unto the sheep gate: and they stood still in the gate of the guard.
leftNotes: 12:39 Or the Old City Gate

units.leftText: The two thanksgiving choirs then stood in the house of God, as did I, along with the half of the officials accompanying me,
units.rightText: So stood the two companies of them that gave thanks in the house of God, and I, and the half of the rulers with me;

units.leftText: as well as the priests with their trumpets — Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah —
units.rightText: and the priests, Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with trumpets;

units.leftText: and also Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. Then the choirs sang out under the direction of Jezrahiah.
units.rightText: and Maaseiah, and Shemaiah, and Eleazar, and Uzzi, and Jehohanan, and Malchijah, and Elam, and Ezer. And the singers sang loud, with Jezrahiah their overseer.

units.leftText: On that day they offered great sacrifices, rejoicing because God had given them great joy. The women and children also rejoiced, so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard from afar. Provisions for Temple Worship
units.rightText: And they offered great sacrifices that day, and rejoiced; for God had made them rejoice with great joy; and the women also and the children rejoiced: so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard even afar off.

units.leftText: And on that same day men were appointed over the rooms that housed the supplies, contributions, firstfruits, and tithes. The portions specified by the Law for the priests and Levites were gathered into these storerooms from the fields of the villages, because Judah rejoiced over the priests and Levites who were serving.
units.rightText: And on that day were men appointed over the chambers for the treasures, for the heave-offerings, for the first-fruits, and for the tithes, to gather into them, according to the fields of the cities, the portions appointed by the law for the priests and Levites: for Judah rejoiced for the priests and for the Levites that waited.

units.leftText: They performed the service of their God and the service of purification, along with the singers and gatekeepers, as David and his son Solomon had prescribed.
units.rightText: And they kept the charge of their God, and the charge of the purification, and so did the singers and the porters, according to the commandment of David, and of Solomon his son.

units.leftText: For long ago, in the days of David and Asaph, there were directors for the singers and for the songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.
units.rightText: For in the days of David and Asaph of old there was a chief of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgiving unto God.

units.leftText: So in the days of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, all Israel contributed the daily portions for the singers and gatekeepers. They also set aside daily portions for the Levites, and the Levites set aside daily portions for the descendants of Aaron.
units.rightText: And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel, and in the days of Nehemiah, gave the portions of the singers and the porters, as every day required: and they set apart that which was for the Levites; and the Levites set apart that which was for the sons of Aaron.

units.leftText: At that time the Book of Moses was read aloud in the hearing of the people, and in it they found the passage stating that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God,
units.rightText: On that day they read in the book of Moses in the audience of the people; and therein was found written, that an Ammonite and a Moabite should not enter into the assembly of God for ever,
leftNotes: 13:1 See Deuteronomy 23:3–6|DEU 23:3-6*.

units.leftText: because they had not met the Israelites with food and water, but had hired Balaam to call down a curse against them (although our God had turned the curse into a blessing).
units.rightText: because they met not the children of Israel with bread and with water, but hired Balaam against them, to curse them: howbeit our God turned the curse into a blessing.

units.leftText: As soon as the people heard this law, they excluded from Israel all of foreign descent. The Temple Cleansed
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when they had heard the law, that they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude.

units.leftText: Now before this, Eliashib the priest, a relative of Tobiah, had been put in charge of the storerooms of the house of our God
units.rightText: Now before this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the chambers of the house of our God, being allied unto Tobiah,

units.leftText: and had prepared for Tobiah a large room where they had previously stored the grain offerings, the frankincense, the temple articles, and the tithes of grain, new wine, and oil prescribed for the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers, along with the contributions for the priests.
units.rightText: had prepared for him a great chamber, where aforetime they laid the meal-offerings, the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tithes of the grain, the new wine, and the oil, which were given by commandment to the Levites, and the singers, and the porters; and the heave-offerings for the priests.

units.leftText: While all this was happening, I was not in Jerusalem, because I had returned to Artaxerxes king of Babylon in the thirty-second year of his reign. Some time later I obtained leave from the king
units.rightText: But in all this time I was not at Jerusalem; for in the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I went unto the king: and after certain days asked I leave of the king,
leftNotes: 13:6 Artaxerxes king of Persia is identified here as the king of Babylon because Persia had conquered the Babylonian Empire.

units.leftText: to return to Jerusalem. Then I discovered the evil that Eliashib had done on behalf of Tobiah by providing him a room in the courts of the house of God.
units.rightText: and I came to Jerusalem, and understood the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, in preparing him a chamber in the courts of the house of God.

units.leftText: And I was greatly displeased and threw all of Tobiah’s household goods out of the room.
units.rightText: And it grieved me sore: therefore I cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah out of the chamber.

units.leftText: Then I ordered that the rooms be purified, and I had the articles of the house of God restored to them, along with the grain offerings and frankincense. Tithes Restored (Leviticus 27:30–34|LEV 27:30-34*; Deuteronomy 14:22–29|DEU 14:22-29*; Deuteronomy 26:1–15|DEU 26:1-15*)
units.rightText: Then I commanded, and they cleansed the chambers: and thither brought I again the vessels of the house of God, with the meal-offerings and the frankincense.

units.leftText: I also learned that because the portions for the Levites had not been given to them, all the Levites and singers responsible for performing the service had gone back to their own fields.
units.rightText: And I perceived that the portions of the Levites had not been given them; so that the Levites and the singers, that did the work, were fled every one to his field.

units.leftText: So I rebuked the officials and asked, “Why has the house of God been neglected?”
units.rightText: Then contended I with the rulers, and said, Why is the house of God forsaken? And I gathered them together, and set them in their place.

units.leftText: and all Judah brought a tenth of the grain, new wine, and oil into the storerooms.
units.rightText: Then brought all Judah the tithe of the grain and the new wine and the oil unto the treasuries.

units.leftText: I appointed as treasurers over the storerooms Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites, with Hanan son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah, to assist them, because they were considered trustworthy. They were responsible for distributing the supplies to their fellow Levites.
units.rightText: And I made treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah: and next to them was Hanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah; for they were counted faithful, and their business was to distribute unto their brethren.

units.leftText: Remember me for this, O my God, and do not blot out my deeds of loving devotion for the house of my God and for its services. The Sabbath Restored (Jeremiah 17:19–27|JER 17:19-27*)
units.rightText: Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God, and for the observances thereof.

units.leftText: In those days I saw people in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath and bringing in grain and loading it on donkeys, along with wine, grapes, and figs. All kinds of goods were being brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. So I warned them against selling food on that day.
units.rightText: In those days saw I in Judah some men treading winepresses on the sabbath, and bringing in sheaves, and lading asses therewith; as also wine, grapes, and figs, and all manner of burdens, which they brought into Jerusalem on the sabbath day: and I testified against them in the day wherein they sold victuals.

units.leftText: Additionally, men of Tyre who lived there were importing fish and all kinds of merchandise and selling them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: There dwelt men of Tyre also therein, who brought in fish, and all manner of wares, and sold on the sabbath unto the children of Judah, and in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Then I rebuked the nobles of Judah and asked, “What is this evil you are doing— profaning the Sabbath day?
units.rightText: Then I contended with the nobles of Judah, and said unto them, What evil thing is this that ye do, and profane the sabbath day?

units.leftText: Did not your forefathers do the same things, so that our God brought all this disaster on us and on this city? And now you are rekindling His wrath against Israel by profaning the Sabbath!”
units.rightText: Did not your fathers thus, and did not our God bring all this evil upon us, and upon this city? yet ye bring more wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath.

units.leftText: When the evening shadows began to fall on the gates of Jerusalem, just before the Sabbath, I ordered that the gates be shut and not opened until after the Sabbath. I posted some of my servants at the gates so that no load could enter on the Sabbath day.
units.rightText: And it came to pass that, when the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the sabbath, I commanded that the doors should be shut, and commanded that they should not be opened till after the sabbath: and some of my servants set I over the gates, that there should no burden be brought in on the sabbath day.

units.leftText: Once or twice, the merchants and those who sell all kinds of goods camped outside Jerusalem,
units.rightText: So the merchants and sellers of all kind of wares lodged without Jerusalem once or twice.

units.leftText: but I warned them, “Why are you camping in front of the wall? If you do it again, I will lay hands on you.” From that time on, they did not return on the Sabbath.
units.rightText: Then I testified against them, and said unto them, Why lodge ye about the wall? if ye do so again, I will lay hands on you. From that time forth came they no more on the sabbath.

units.leftText: Then I instructed the Levites to purify themselves and guard the gates in order to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember me for this as well, O my God, and show me mercy according to Your abundant loving devotion. Intermarriage Forbidden (Ezra 9:1–4|EZR 9:1-4*)
units.rightText: And I commanded the Levites that they should purify themselves, and that they should come and keep the gates, to sanctify the sabbath day. Remember unto me, O my God, this also, and spare me according to the greatness of thy lovingkindness.

units.leftText: In those days I also saw Jews who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
units.rightText: In those days also saw I the Jews that had married women of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab:

units.leftText: Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod or of the other peoples, but could not speak the language of Judah.
units.rightText: and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews’ language, but according to the language of each people.

units.leftText: I rebuked them and called down curses on them. I beat some of these men and pulled out their hair.
units.rightText: And I contended with them, and cursed them, and smote certain of them, and plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God, saying, Ye shall not give your daughters unto their sons, nor take their daughters for your sons, or for yourselves.

units.leftText: Did not King Solomon of Israel sin in matters like this? There was not a king like him among many nations, and he was loved by his God, who made him king over all Israel— yet foreign women drew him into sin.
units.rightText: Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? yet among many nations was there no king like him, and he was beloved of his God, and God made him king over all Israel: nevertheless even him did foreign women cause to sin.

units.leftText: Must we now hear that you too are doing all this terrible evil and acting unfaithfully against our God by marrying foreign women?”
units.rightText: Shall we then hearken unto you to do all this great evil, to trespass against our God in marrying foreign women?

units.leftText: Even one of the sons of Jehoiada son of Eliashib the high priest had become a son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite. Therefore I drove him away from me.
units.rightText: And one of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite: therefore I chased him from me.

units.leftText: Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.
units.rightText: Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood, and the covenant of the priesthood, and of the Levites.

units.leftText: Thus I purified the priests and Levites from everything foreign, and I assigned specific duties to each of the priests and Levites.
units.rightText: Thus cleansed I them from all foreigners, and appointed charges for the priests and for the Levites, every one in his work;

units.leftText: I also arranged for contributions of wood at the appointed times, and for the firstfruits. Remember me, O my God, with favor.
units.rightText: and for the wood-offering, at times appointed, and for the first-fruits. Remember me, O my God, for good.
